papers.title: Validity of Psychological Assessment: Validation of Inferences From Persons' Responses and Performances as Scientific Inquiry Into Score Meaning
papers.abstract_snippet: Landmark paper on construct validity arguing that validity is a unified concept encompassing content, criterion, and construct aspects. All validation is construct validation — the evidential and consequential bases of test interpretation and use.

papers.title: Challenging the Validity of Personality Tests for Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Challenges whether standard human personality tests produce valid measurements when administered to LLMs, demonstrating systematic failures in reliability and construct validity of such assessments.

papers.title: A psychometric framework for evaluating and shaping personality traits in large language models
papers.abstract_snippet: Develops a psychometric framework specifically designed for evaluating LLM personality traits, addressing reliability, validity, and measurement invariance concerns unique to language model assessment.

papers.title: Psychometric Evaluation of LLM Embeddings for Personality Assessment
papers.abstract_snippet: Evaluates whether LLM embeddings can serve as valid personality assessment tools using psychometric criteria including internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and convergent validity.

papers.title: Decoding LLM Personality Measurement: Forced-Choice Approaches
papers.abstract_snippet: Investigates forced-choice item formats for measuring LLM personality, comparing them to Likert-scale approaches and demonstrating superior measurement properties for forced-choice designs.

papers.title: Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract_snippet: Applies cognitive psychology experimental paradigms to GPT-3, finding that the model shows human-like biases in some domains but systematic deviations in others, raising questions about validity of psychological measurement applied to LLMs.

papers.title: Whose Opinions Do Language Models Reflect?
papers.authors: Santurkar, S., Durmus, E., Ladhak, F., Lee, C., Liang, P., & Hashimoto, T.
papers.abstract_snippet: Investigates whose opinions and values are encoded in language model outputs, finding systematic biases toward particular demographic groups and political orientations, undermining claims of neutral measurement.

papers.title: Systematic Bias in LLMs: Discrepant Response Patterns in Binary vs. Continuous Formats
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates systematic discrepancies in LLM responses between binary and continuous response formats, showing that format choice fundamentally alters measured attitudes and values.

papers.title: Established Psychometric vs. Ecologically Valid Questionnaires: Rethinking Assessments in LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Contrasts established psychometric instruments with ecologically valid alternatives for LLM assessment, arguing that standard questionnaires may lack validity when applied to non-human subjects.

papers.title: Construct Validity in Psychological Tests
papers.authors: Cronbach, L. J. & Meehl, P. E.
papers.abstract_snippet: Classic paper establishing the concept of construct validity in psychological testing, arguing that tests must be embedded in a nomological network of theoretical relationships to demonstrate validity.

papers.title: Validating the Interpretations and Uses of Test Scores
papers.abstract_snippet: Presents an argument-based approach to validation, emphasizing that validity refers to the interpretations and uses of test scores rather than the test itself. Influential framework for modern validity theory.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Have a Personality?
papers.abstract_snippet: Investigates whether LLMs exhibit stable personality traits using standard personality inventories, finding evidence of personality-like patterns but questioning whether these reflect genuine psychological constructs.
